# Recreate the animated phantom owl — complete implementation and agent handoff

Effect snapshot: **2026-11-11, `pause-after-5-to-7-12`**, preserved in the **`organized-project-13`** folder layout. This is the current effect after the user requested that all animation settings be recorded. It replaces the earlier pre-animation snapshot and its reference frames. The folder reorganization changes module/asset locations and extracts the existing vertex shader into its own file; the effect and its numeric settings are unchanged. See [the project map](../README.md) for the current structure. The root URL and the old `/owl-flight/` URL both redirect to `/app/`, preserving query parameters.

This document is a standalone recreation package: explanations, exact parameters, complete runtime source, preserved original shader, exact owl PNG, current screenshots, dependency hashes, and an extractor. A separate agent can reconstruct the effect from this Markdown alone. The first extraction needs internet access for two pinned Three.js modules, or a local copy of those modules. Running the reconstructed app needs no external services, API keys, npm install, build system, image generation, or model download.

**Agent handoff:** read the prose and source sections, then execute the extractor. Decode the large base64 appendix programmatically rather than loading it into model context. Reproduce the snapshot before making changes. The file-marked source blocks are authoritative if an explanatory example is abbreviated. Do not replace this implementation with a primitive-built owl, physical feather material, opaque photograph, new palette, or UI.

## 1. What this version should look and feel like

The entire viewport is white, with no visible text or controls. One barn owl appears as broad, noisy strands of colored light. Features emerge and disappear through the color. Both wings make deep, smooth strokes, including movement along the screen-normal Z direction. A rounded image-derived shell gives the wings thickness. An airy wake drifts off the moving wings, breaks into smaller wisps, and dissipates.

The final motion contract is precise:

- Every flap has the same maximum depth. Randomness changes speed and grouping, not stroke strength, shape variants, or left/right asymmetry.
- Logical cycles contain **1–3 flaps**, with no pause or neutral stop at an ordinary cycle boundary.
- Count flaps across those cycles. After **exactly 5, 6, or 7 completed flaps**, selected randomly and inclusively, recover to neutral and pause for **0.85 seconds**. Then choose another 5–7-flap target.
- Each full flap takes **1.20–1.95 seconds**. These are cinematic timing choices, not measured barn owl flight data.
- The initial neutral hold is **0.8 seconds**. This startup hold is separate from the recurring 0.85-second pauses.
- Intermediate recoveries continue directly into the next upstroke. The last recovery before a scheduled pause ends at neutral without an extra up-and-down rebound.
- The wake carries color away. It does not use delayed owl copies, spring back to the wing, or stretch directly with instantaneous wing velocity.

The color uses the original shader's accumulating RGB calculations. White space, partial disappearance, and fine noisy detail are intentional. The user's former “80% color” instruction is represented by the recorded contribution coefficients; it is **not** an 80% alpha value or a guarantee that 80% of pixels are colored.

## 3. Source image, UVs, and the real limits of feature detail

The exact source PNG is embedded in this document. Its SHA-256 is `fad19b6a83a0160a116b662711ed1b8ba190f00cfe376e3671d93073f67757af`. It was generated using the original cropped barn owl photograph for appearance and a generated glide/bank reference for complete flight anatomy. The generation prompt is included below. Generation is nondeterministic; use the embedded PNG for exact recreation. Earlier turnaround and state sheets are historical references and are **not** combined by the current runtime.

The final owl has a heart-shaped facial disk, dark eyes, pale breast, and broad feathered wings. Unseen surfaces in generated references are artistic estimates. No calibrated multiview reconstruction, anatomical mesh, or cross-view UV unwrap exists here.

### UV registration

The source image, relief, and normals use the same planar image-space coordinates:

```javascript
const u = (x + 0.5) / width;
const v = 1 - (y + 0.5) / height;
```

Image arrays start at the top left; shader UVs start at the bottom left. Generated `DataTexture` objects use `flipY = true`. Source coverage, normals, and relief are sampled using the unchanged `vUv`. The vertex shader moves the shell while carrying those UVs with it. A separate procedural coordinate is distorted for the liquid color. Do not independently warp or crop the source and feature maps.

Both sides of the shell reuse the same UV image. This creates a useful front-view illusion but does not supply a correct underside/back appearance or hidden features at arbitrary camera angles.

### Why the face and feathers can resemble a faint image overlay

Their recognizable detail is still largely a 2D contrast signal:

```javascript
brightness = (red * .2126 + green * .7152 + blue * .0722) / 255;
```

These are weighted **encoded image RGB values**, without sRGB-to-linear decoding. They are an appearance signal, not measured albedo or depth. Eyes, feather markings, and shadows all affect the result.

The map builder adds approximate broad volume:

```text
head   = exp(-((u-.50)/.075)^2 - ((v-.69)/.23)^2)
breast = exp(-((u-.50)/.068)^2 - ((v-.43)/.27)^2)
wings  = exp(-((v-.56)/.20)^2) * exp(-((u-.50)/.55)^2)
relief = .52*head + .35*breast + .10*wings + .045*brightness
```

Broad relief is computed only where source alpha exceeds `180/255`. Two-pixel finite differences derive normal slopes, multiplied by `.09`. Outside-silhouette neighbors use the current height instead of background zero. Normal encoding is `RGB = normal*.5+.5`; axes are +X right, +Y up, +Z toward the viewer. This is an image/view-space estimate, not a calibrated tangent-space normal map.

| Texture | R | G | B | A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Source | Original image R | Original image G | Original image B | Silhouette |
| Normal | Encoded normal X | Encoded normal Y | Encoded normal Z | Source alpha |
| Relief | Normalized estimated height | Encoded-RGB brightness | Zero | Source alpha |

In the surface shader, `feather = 1 - relief.g`. The term `feather * pool * .15` adds faint neutral density; `.9801` scales an additional colored detail sample. Normal XY offsets the color coordinates by `.028`, and relief offsets Y by `.09`. These effects make color bend and vary around apparent features.

**The face is still geometrically flat.** Head/breast relief affects shader coordinates, but vertex relief and shell thickness are multiplied by a wing mask that is zero at the center. Eyes, beak, and individual feathers have no independently modeled depth. Feather texture also makes a small wing vertex displacement. The photo's RGB is not shown as a skin, but grayscale detail can still look like a translucent image. Better localized facial/feather relief would be a future improvement; it is not secretly present in this snapshot.

## 4. Exact color and strand settings

`phantom-color.glsl` preserves the original accumulating RGB-loop coordinates. Each channel starts from the previous channel's already-modified `st`. Resetting coordinates inside the loop caused the unwanted saturated rainbow prototype. The original mouse-dependent subtraction is now a fixed `vec2(.5)`. There is no mouse or click input.

```glsl
for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    st -= vec2(.5);                  // accumulates; never reset st here
    st.x *= .3 * (u_resolution.x/u_resolution.y) / (16.0/9.0);
    z -= 1.0;
    l = length(st);
    float denom = (rnd/2.2) * sin(l*50.0 - 2.0*z);
    st *= (denom < 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0) / max(abs(denom), .00001);
    c[i] = fract(.01/max(length(st-.5), .00001)) * 5.0/(1.0+l*3.0);
}
return clamp(c*9.0+l, 0.0, 1.0);
```

`rnd` is the original `fract(sin(dot(st,st))*43758.5453123)` evaluated before the loop. A signed reciprocal replaces the original undefined negative-base `pow(x,-1)` operation. `highp`, initialized variables, and denominator guards make the working version numerically defined. These adaptations do not alter the preserved original files.

| Parameter | Current value |
|---|---|
| Shader reference resolution | `(16,9)`, independent of viewport |
| Color clock | `time * .075` |
| Smooth-noise octave weights | `.57, .28, .15` |
| Domain spatial scale | `(2.0,1.3)` |
| Flow displacement | `(flow-.5)*.34` |
| Density contour scale / blend | `.42` / `.78` |
| Vertical drift of contours | `sin(clock*.7)*.05` |
| Main color contribution | `4.455` |
| Colored feature contribution | `.9801` |
| Neutral feature contribution | `.15` |
| Primary strand samples | 3, plus one detail sample on the owl |
| Source alpha coverage | `smoothstep(.55,.96,owl.a)` |
| Pool | `smoothstep(.30,.67,liquid)` |
| Visibility | `coverage*smoothstep(.23,.54,liquid)` |
| Color absorption cap | `.7` per channel |
| Side-wall density multiplier | `1 + v_edge*.12` |
| Fragment discard threshold | Coverage or final alpha below `.005` |

The liquid construction is shared conceptually by the owl and its detached field:

```glsl
vec2 p = fieldUv * vec2(2.0,1.3);
vec2 flow = vec2(fbm(p+vec2(clock,-clock*.33)),
                 fbm(p+vec2(-clock*.4,clock*.6)+9.2));
float liquid = fbm(p*1.4 + flow*2.3 + vec2(-clock*.65,clock*.2));
vec2 curved = fieldUv + (flow-.5)*.34 + normal.xy*.028
              + vec2(0.0,surface.x*.09);
curved.y = mix(curved.y,.5+(liquid-.5)*.42+normal.y*.03,.78);
curved.y += sin(clock*.7)*.05;
```

The detached field omits the normal/relief terms. `strandColor` samples the original color function at `curved`, then at offsets `(.08, .13+sin(clock*.43)*.025)` with time `clock+.65`, and `(-.07, -.13+cos(clock*.37)*.025)` with time `clock+1.3`. It selects the strongest **whole RGB sample** by absorption weights `(.2126,.7152,.0722)`, rather than adding samples or independently choosing channels.

The surface output is `1 - clamp(absorption*(1+v_edge*.12),0,.7)`, blended over white with the visibility alpha. The cloud uses the same `strandColor`, gain `4.455`, and cap `.7`; its transported density and porous edges control how much is visible. Equal peak color strength does not mean every cloud pixel has identical opacity to an owl pixel.

Historical tuning reached main gain `1 → 1.20 → 1.65 → 2.475 → 4.455`, detail `.22 → .264 → .363 → .5445 → .9801`, contour scale `1.8 → 1.6 → 1.3 → .95 → .42`, spatial scale `(3.3,2.1) → (2.0,1.3)`, and primary strand count `1 → 3`. The rightmost values are the current defaults; earlier values are not alternative instructions.

## 5. Wing volume and the screen-normal stroke

The owl is one mesh derived from its alpha image, with upper/lower skins joined at active-cell edges. It is not assembled from separate spheres, feather primitives, or a skeleton. The nominal source mesh has **256 columns × 96 rows**. Cells are included when their center source alpha exceeds `140/255`.

An approximate contour-distance field is computed in object units with `dx=1/256`, `dy=(imageHeight/imageWidth)/96` and diagonal distance `hypot(dx,dy)`. The roundness attribute is `min(1,distance/.035)`. Thickness tapers through `sqrt(roundness)` so the wing closes toward feather edges instead of showing long extruded side walls. For this PNG the built geometry has 53,250 vertices and 49,316 triangles.

The following are local normalized mesh units unless indicated. The image aspect is exactly 3.

| Quantity | Current expression |
|---|---|
| Wing participation | `smoothstep(.065,.17,abs(position.x))` |
| Distance from shoulder | `max(abs(position.x)-.085,0)` |
| Outer-wing weighting | `smoothstep(.20,.48,abs(position.x))` |
| Stroke/wrist blend | `mix(stroke,wrist,outer*.55)` |
| Depth/tip-depth blend | `mix(depth,depthTip,outer*.65)` |
| X folding projection | `cos(angle*.60)*cos(depthAngle)` |
| Y stroke | `reach*sin(angle)*imageAspect*wing*.68` |
| Z stroke | `reach*sin(depthAngle)*wing` |
| Chord coordinate | `(uv.y-.56)/.39` |
| Cup | `max(0,1-chord*chord)` |
| Downstroke power | `max(-stroke,0)` |
| Camber | `cup*(.045+.075*power)*wing` |
| Trailing-edge twist | `(uv.y-.56)*outer*sin(angle)*.19*wing` |
| Image relief vertex offset | `relief.r*.045*wing` |
| Additional cupping Y | `cup*sin(angle)*outer*.075*imageAspect*wing` |
| Cupping X tuck | `-side*cup*outer*power*.018*wing` |
| Tip-fold X tuck | `-side*reach*fold*outer*.13*wing` |
| Tip-fold Z lift | `cup*fold*outer*.03*wing` |

The skins use opposite `a_shell` signs. Their local half-thickness and offset are:

```glsl
float thickness = (.025 + .055*(1.0-outer) + .018*power)*wing;
float profile = (.35+.65*sqrt(cup))*sqrt(a_roundness);
vec3 shellNormal = normalize(vec3(-side*sin(depthAngle),
                                  -sin(angle)*.35, cos(depthAngle)));
vec3 offset = shellNormal * a_shell * thickness * profile;
p += vec3(offset.x, offset.y*imageAspect, offset.z);
```

This is an artistic shell offset, not an exact geometric normal solution. The face remains flat because `wing=0` there. Surface normals used by the color shader are still image-space estimates and are not recalculated from the deformed shell. The geometry is sufficient for this frontal phantom effect, not for a camera orbit around an anatomical bird.

## 6. Final motion numbers and sequencing

All timing is in simulation seconds. Angle-like values feed `sin`/`cos` in radians; they are not world-space distances.

| Parameter | Final value |
|---|---:|
| Cycle count | Shuffled bag of `1,2,3` |
| Flaps before a pause | `5 + floor(random()*3)` → 5, 6, or 7 |
| Remaining-flap cap on a cycle | `min(nextCount(), pauseAfter-flapsSincePause)` |
| Full-flap duration | Uniform `[1.20,1.95)` s |
| Gap between individual flaps | `0` |
| Ordinary cycle-boundary pause | `0` |
| Scheduled glide after 5–7 flaps | `.85` s |
| Initial hold | `.8` s |
| Upper/lower key values | `.59` / `-1.02` |
| Fixed amplitude | `1.06` |
| Maximum downward stroke | `-1.0812` (`-1.02*1.06`) |
| Depth multiplier | `1.14` |
| Maximum downward depth parameter | `-1.232568` (`-1.02*1.06*1.14`) |
| Wingtip gain | `.94` |
| Wingtip phase delay | `.08` of that beat's duration |
| Fold strength | `.24` |
| Fold envelope | `(height/-1.02)^2` |
| Body heave | `-stroke*.009` |
| Velocity finite difference | Samples at `t-.004` and `t+.004`, divide by `.008` |

### How continuous strokes work

For a beat starting at absolute time `b` with duration `L`, append only the stroke extremes:

```javascript
keys.push([b + L*.24, .59], [b + L*.56, -1.02]);
tipKeys.push([b + L*.32, .59], [b + L*.64, -1.02]);
```

The next beat adds its next upper extreme. There is **no neutral key at an ordinary beat or cycle boundary**. Interpolate each interval with the clamped quintic `s(x)=x*x*x*(x*(x*6-15)+10)`. Velocity and acceleration go to zero at stroke extremes, while the intervening recovery crosses neutral in motion. A look-ahead condition generates future keys before evaluating a final recovery, avoiding an accidental fallback to neutral when the next cycle has not been generated yet.

Only when the cumulative flap target is met does the scheduler append `[end,0]`, add a `.85`-second glide segment, and append `[glideEnd,0]`. The final downstroke therefore recovers directly to neutral and holds there. There is no extra small upstroke followed by a dip. Reset the cumulative counter and draw a new 5–7 target after the pause.

The 1–3-cycle count is capped if needed to hit the exact total. For example, a proposed three-flap cycle becomes one flap when five have been completed toward a six-flap target. It must never overshoot the target and pause after eight or nine flaps. A cycle grouping has no separate visual pause; the count across cycles determines the glide.

Left and right wings use identical pose values. Earlier depth variants, light correction strokes, random amplitudes, side-to-side phase shifts, and asymmetric banks were removed at the user's request. The normal slow whole-owl drift remains:

```javascript
x = Math.sin(t*.10) * viewportAspect * .11;
y = Math.sin(t*.18) * .08 - stroke*.009;
rotationZ = Math.sin(t*.10) * .025; // motion.bank is zero in this version
```

### Randomness and repeatability

The local PRNG is `state=(imul(state,1664525)+1013904223)>>>0`, with output `state/4294967296`. The seed defaults to `12345` for a fixed-time URL, and to a browser cryptographic random integer for normal playback. Supply `?seed=12345` for a repeatable live sequence, or `?time=...&seed=12345` to freeze a time. Zero seeds are internally mapped to 1. Keep PRNG call order unchanged when reproducing the exact schedule.

The renderer caps each real frame's elapsed increment at `.05` seconds, so a stalled tab does not jump far ahead. Slow devices can run behind wall-clock time. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` stops automatic time advancement; explicit fixed-time captures still work.

### Attached pigment slip

Small color movement still attached to the feathers uses a first-order relaxation, not a spring:

```javascript
step = 1/120;
response = 1 - Math.exp(-3.2*step);
target = [-strokeVelocity*.035, -depthVelocity*.030];
offset += (target-offset)*response;
```

This response cannot overshoot a stationary zero target. The surface's wing weighting is `smoothstep(.075,.32,abs(uv.x-.5))`; its shoulder is `(.5+side*.09,.60)`. Offsets use X/Y coefficients `.32` and `.65`, plus a rotational term `.65` around that shoulder. The face stays anchored. This small attached slip is separate from the detached persistent cloud.

## 7. Airy cloud transport, opacity, and width

The wake is an approximate 2D advected field, not a pressure-solved fluid simulation. It has persistent velocity and pigment buffers, small rotating disturbances, diffusion, local breakup, ambient lift, and decay. It contains no stored historical owl silhouettes or delayed wing meshes.

### Passes and state

Each simulation step is at most `1/30` second. Three emitters per wing, at absolute local X spans `.22`, `.33`, `.43`, follow the same stroke, cup, and fold calculations as the wing surface. Their projected screen-UV differences divided by `dt` supply velocity. There are six emitters total; their positions describe a representative mid-chord region rather than every feather.

1. Render the **current** owl over white into a source target with a depth buffer.
2. Backtrace the previous velocity. Add localized wing impulses, swirl, smaller eddies, and ambient lift. Transport accumulated displacement alongside velocity.
3. Backtrace pigment using the updated velocity, diffuse/decay it, and inject color density from blurred live source samples near moving wings.
4. Draw the cloud over white, then draw the owl with its depth-tested shell.

The velocity texture stores velocity XY in **RG** and accumulated displacement XY in **BA**. Encoding is `encoded=value/.9+zero`, decoding is `(encoded-zero)*.9`. Both are clamped to `[-.44,.44]` in the simulation. A zero of `.5` is exact for half-float storage; the unsigned-byte fallback uses `128/255`. Reset writes numeric RGBA with a fullscreen shader. A translucent renderer clear would premultiply RGB by alpha and corrupt the data.

Two velocity targets and two dye targets alternate after each pass. Resolution is 512 pixels wide and `clamp(round(512/aspect),192,768)` high, using linear filtering. Half-float targets are used when `EXT_color_buffer_float` is available; unsigned-byte fallback has coarser transport and can look different. The source has depth; velocity and dye targets do not.

### Exact velocity values

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Advection coordinate clamp | `.001` to `.999` |
| Velocity decay | `exp(-dt*1.05)` |
| Emitter falloff | `exp(-dot(delta,delta)/.0045)` |
| Force activation by speed | `smoothstep(.01,.12,speed)` |
| Wing velocity gain / force clamp | `.80` / `[-.32,.32]` per component |
| Force response | `1-exp(-dt*5.5)` |
| Tangent denominator minimum | `.015` |
| Tip swirl coefficient | `.95`; opposite handedness on the two sides |
| Main eddy spatial frequency | `39` |
| Main eddy time drift | `(.38,-.31)*time` |
| Fine eddy scale / weight | `1.91` / `.55` |
| Fine eddy time drift | `(-.21,.27)*time` |
| Occupancy | `smoothstep(.002,.08,length(dye.rgb))` |
| Eddy strength | `energy*.85 + .022*occupied` |
| Ambient X acceleration | `.005*sin(time*.27)/aspect` |
| Ambient Y acceleration | `.016` |

Distances are corrected with `metric(delta)=delta*vec2(aspect,1)`. Accumulated displacement follows `transportedPreviousDisplacement + velocity*dt`. The display samples color at `screenUV - displacement`. It does not warp color by instantaneous velocity, which previously made the field stretch and recoil like an elastic sheet.

### Exact density and display values

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Four-neighbor diffusion | `1-exp(-dt*8)` |
| Breakup noise frequency / drift | `43`, `(.24,-.35)*time` |
| Dye decay | `exp(-dt*(.85+breakup*.6))` |
| Injection falloff | `exp(-dot(delta,delta)/.0120)` |
| Injection speed activation | `smoothstep(.012,.18,speed)` |
| Source sampling | 3×3 samples, spacing `3.5*texel`, averaged |
| Injection modulation | `.45+.75*noise(metric(uv)*57 + time*(.3,-.2))` |
| Injection cap / response | `min(injection,1.5)` / `1-exp(-dt*5)` |
| Stored dye clamp | `0` to `.7` |
| Display mass | `max(dye.r,max(dye.g,dye.b))` |
| Base density | `smoothstep(.004,.095,mass)` |
| Porosity coordinates | `metric(uv-displacement)*37 + time*(.12,-.18)` |
| Porosity noise scales / weights | `1` and `2.07` with offset `5.3`; `.65` and `.35` |
| Porosity threshold | `smoothstep(.22,.70,pockets)` |
| Dense-core preservation | Mix porosity toward 1 with `smoothstep(.14,.30,mass)` |
| Cloud color gain / cap | `4.455` / `.7`, shared with wing color |

Transported dye controls density. The display regenerates fine color structure using the shared original shader at transported coordinates. Directly displaying diffused RGB made the cloud muddy/brown. The color pattern's image-scale frame is established once after reset and does not follow later owl translation, so detached wisps are not pulled with the owl. The field's RGBA output alpha is 1; visible transparency against white is represented as `white - clampedAbsorption*density`, with porous edges and fading mass.

Airiness comes from smaller localized forces, weaker coupling, persistent transport without elastic return, smaller eddies, porous edges, and faster dissipation. Width comes from emission spread, advection, blur, and diffusion; it is not a broad duplicate wing silhouette. The brightest core keeps the wing's color-strength ceiling while sparse edges disappear.

## 8. Camera, render state, and simulation replay

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Camera | Perspective, vertical FOV 28°, Z=4, near `.1`, far `20` |
| Owl width | `min(viewportAspect*1.4,2.3)` |
| Owl XYZ scale | `(w,w*imageHeight/imageWidth,w)` |
| Renderer | Antialias enabled, alpha disabled, white clear color |
| Pixel ratio | `min(devicePixelRatio,2)` |
| Automatic clearing | Disabled; passes clear explicitly |
| Owl material | Transparent, depth test/write enabled; default front-side rendering |
| Owl render order / culling | `100` / frustum culling disabled for vertex motion |
| Source image filtering | Linear min/mag, no generated mipmaps |
| Surface texture sizes | 2172 × 724 |

Update the camera's world matrix before projecting emitters or the initial color frame. Without it, the first projected frame can contain non-finite coordinates. `renderAt(t)` simulates forward in small steps, resets cloud history when rewinding, updates attached pigment and pose, and renders cloud then owl. Resizing reallocates/reset buffers and replays to the requested time. Long-history replay and synchronous map generation can be expensive; this prototype has not implemented workers or production history truncation.

For consistent screenshots, call `renderAt(0)` and then `renderAt(target)` after stopping the animation loop. This initializes the color frame at neutral and gives each frame a repeatable wake history. Changing only `u_time`, or calling `renderer.render(scene,camera)` directly, does not reproduce the wake. A page loaded directly at a nonzero `?time=` can establish the detached color frame at that pose; use the QA script's time-zero initialization when comparing the supplied references.

## 9. Verification and troubleshooting

### Numeric motion check

```bash
node tools/verify-snapshot.mjs --motion-only
```

This checks 229 pauses, 1,404 full-depth flaps, and 537 continuous cycle joins across eight deterministic seeds. It verifies inclusive 5/6/7 counts, 0.85-second neutral holds, 1–3-flap logical cycles, fixed deepest depth, smooth boundaries, and deterministic sampling. It checks behavioral invariants rather than screenshot resemblance.

### Browser capture and reconstruction check

Start the static server, then start a dedicated temporary Chrome instance. On macOS:

```bash
"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
  --headless --no-first-run --user-data-dir=/tmp/phantom-snapshot-chrome \
  --remote-debugging-port=9223 about:blank
```

On Linux or Windows, substitute the installed Chrome/Chromium executable. Use a separate profile from your personal browser. In another terminal, run:

```bash
node tools/verify-snapshot.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/app/ /tmp/phantom-snapshot
```

The tool records full downstroke, recovery, pause, resume, and mobile PNGs plus a JSON report. It checks all compiled shader programs, source dimensions, finite geometry and color-frame coordinates, the white background, and absence of visible text and browser errors. It disables browser cache in that QA session and uses seed 12345. Stop the dedicated QA browser afterward; leave the preview server running if someone is using it.

The older `verify-phantom.mjs` is retained for optional map PNG exports and historical checks. For current motion references use `verify-snapshot.mjs`: it invokes the full cloud renderer for desktop and mobile and captures the current schedule. Runtime map data can also be exported through an offscreen canvas without changing the application:

```javascript
const texture = __owl.maps.normal; // or .relief
const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
canvas.width = texture.image.width;
canvas.height = texture.image.height;
canvas.getContext('2d').putImageData(new ImageData(
  new Uint8ClampedArray(texture.image.data), canvas.width, canvas.height), 0, 0);
const pngDataUrl = canvas.toDataURL('image/png');
```

Map PNG RGB can change slightly at low alpha during canvas export; runtime consumes the original data arrays. Compare map alignment and decoded normals in opaque pixels, not undefined RGB in transparent pixels.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Inspect |
|---|---|
| Saturated rainbow silhouette | RGB coordinate reset, new palette, changed gain, or color-space conversion |
| Brown/muddy clouds | Direct display of diffused RGB instead of shared color shader |
| Elastic wake or abrupt pullback | Instantaneous velocity used as displacement, a spring response, or moving the detached color frame with the owl |
| Frame-delay ghosts | Historical owl textures/meshes being composited instead of advected density |
| Neutral stop between every flap | A neutral key or gap was inserted at an ordinary beat boundary |
| Pause after too many flaps | Cycle length was not capped by remaining flaps before the pause |
| Different depths at different speeds | Random amplitude/depth or altered stroke variants were reintroduced |
| Paper-like wing edge | Missing second skin, contour taper, camber, depth projection, or alpha shell |
| Long rectangular side-wall streaks | Missing contour-distance taper toward the feather edge |
| Face still looks flat | Current feature representation is image-based; the face has no geometric displacement |
| Features slide relative to feathers | Mismatched UVs, crops, dimensions, or flip conventions |
| Gray cloud / corrupt color frame | Camera matrix not initialized, non-finite frame uniform, or corrupt numeric RGBA reset |
| Buffer slowly drifts with no input | Incorrect numeric zero for the render-target type |
| No animation | Fixed `?time=`, reduced-motion preference, or paused QA animation loop |
| Wrong wake after seeking | Time changed without resetting/replaying simulation |
| Module/include failure | Missing `.mjs` files or `phantom-color.glsl`; file URL instead of HTTP |

### Standalone handoff test performed for this snapshot

The extractor in this document was executed into a new empty temporary directory, using the local pinned vendor modules as its optional offline cache. All **manifest-listed source/image artifacts and both Three.js modules** matched their expected bytes and SHA-256 hashes. The extraction also restored the reconstruction manifest itself. The initial-network download branch is specified by pinned URLs and hashes; this test used the offline cache.

That reconstructed project was served on a separate temporary port and checked with its own extracted `verify-snapshot.mjs`. All six WebGL programs were runnable, geometry and the color frame were finite, the background was white with no visible text, and browser errors were empty. The numeric checks passed for 229 pauses, 1,404 fixed-depth flaps, and 537 uninterrupted cycle joins. The capture report and all five PNGs matched the current project's captures **byte-for-byte on the same machine/browser/GPU**. This is evidence of a complete handoff, not a promise of pixel-identical noise on every GPU.

The reorganization changes paths and moves the existing wing vertex shader into its own file. Its shader arithmetic, animation numbers, source images, wing geometry, and cloud behavior remain unchanged. The current guide embeds the reorganized source and paths. The original shader and its preserved backup remain identical.


## 10. Applying the technique to another owl or object

Keep the reusable parts separate: an isolated image and feature maps; subject-specific deformation/volume; shared color arithmetic; motion; and emitted cloud transport. The current single-view owl is a concrete instance of this pipeline, not an automatic reconstruction system.

1. Collect references in the species/object folder and record which surfaces are visible or missing. Preserve original photographs. Choose one canonical full-subject pose for the runtime input.
2. Use or generate a sharp neutral image with real transparency. Keep lighting soft, margins clear, and important landmarks visible. Do not bake rainbow color, fog, a checkerboard, shadows, or the phantom effect into the PNG.
3. Save exact dimensions, image bytes, prompt, references, and SHA-256. A prompt alone cannot reproduce a generated image. More reference angles help review anatomy but do not automatically establish surface correspondence.
4. Derive source coverage, weighted brightness, approximate height, and normals from that **same** image. All maps must share crop, orientation, dimensions, and UV convention. Keep provenance explicit.
5. Replace the owl's broad Gaussian forms with shapes placed at the new subject's landmarks. Preserve the color functions while tuning feature contribution and scale.
6. Replace the owl-specific wing mask, shoulder locations, chord, shell offset, and stroke deformation. The alpha contour builder is reusable; the feather-specific vertex equations are not universal.
7. Attach emitter positions to the new moving surface and project their displacement into screen UV per second. Six wing emitters and their shader loop count are owl-specific. If there are no moving parts, disable emission or supply an explicitly designed source of disturbance.
8. Reuse the shared palette and advected-density rendering. Keep density sparse enough to reveal and lose the object. Build new reference captures after tuning.
9. Store source, maps, source code, all coefficients, seed, viewport, and complete wake replay procedure. Verify extraction into a clean directory as done here.

An optional generation prompt template:

```text
One detailed [SUBJECT] in [POSE], viewed from [CAMERA].
Use reference 1 for identity/material and reference 2 for silhouette/pose.
Preserve [IMPORTANT LANDMARKS]. Whole subject visible, generous margins.
Soft neutral lighting and a truly transparent background.
No text, border, scenery, shadows, fog, glow, checkerboard, or shader effects.
The image will drive registered silhouette and approximate feature maps.
```

For another owl, fit the facial disk, breast, shoulders, wing span, and feather contour to that image. A species with ear tufts or a different face silhouette needs those landmarks in the source. Do not merely recolor this barn owl and claim a new anatomical model.

### Example: rounded stone

Replace owl broad relief with a centered dome:

```javascript
const dome = Math.exp(-(((u-.50)/.28)**2) - (((v-.50)/.32)**2));
relief[k] = .65*dome + .035*brightness;
```

Use a plane or a subject-appropriate inflated alpha shell. Remove the owl-specific deformation and emitters. A constant wing mask of zero alone would also remove the current shell's thickness, so author the desired stone volume explicitly. The same color shader can remain active over a stationary shape.

### Example: flower

```javascript
let petals = 0;
for (let i=0; i<8; i++) {
  const a = i*Math.PI*2/8;
  const cx = .5+Math.cos(a)*.21, cy = .5+Math.sin(a)*.21;
  petals = Math.max(petals, Math.exp(-(((u-cx)/.13)**2)-(((v-cy)/.13)**2)));
}
const center = Math.exp(-(((u-.5)/.12)**2)-(((v-.5)/.12)**2));
relief[k] = .40*center + .20*petals + .025*brightness;
```

Fit those locations to the actual image. Petal motion needs different pivots and emitter positions; do not retain the owl's flight scheduler. For a face, manually placed brow/cheek/socket relief can improve structure, but dark markings should not automatically become dents. Negative heights require deliberate remapping before the current unsigned-byte packing.

### Other views and animation states

The larger game scope still includes flying, takeoff, touchdown, rest, walking, and idle. **Only procedural frontal flight and brief neutral glides are implemented here.** There is no walking, blink, landing contact, takeoff transition, or state machine hidden in the snapshot.

For each additional view/state, produce aligned image/coverage/relief/normal sets and consistent scale, pivots, orientation, and subject identity. Walking needs foot contacts; takeoff needs push-off and wing unfolding; touchdown needs flare, feet contact, impact, and folding. Idle/rest need their own intentional small motions. A normal map from a wings-folded pose will not fit a spread-wing image. Independent generated frames may flicker or change anatomy; use authored correspondence or an offline common surface when consistency is required. The final display may remain shader-driven even if an offline model is used to bake consistent maps.

### `references/shaders/shaderRef.glsl`

<!-- FILE: references/shaders/shaderRef.glsl -->
```glsl
#ifdef GL_ES
precision mediump float;
#endif

uniform vec2 u_resolution;
uniform vec2 u_mouse;
uniform float u_time;

uniform vec2 u_click;
uniform float u_clickTime;

#define t u_time
#define r u_resolution

float random(vec2 st) {
    return fract(sin(dot(st, st))* 43758.5453123);
}


//Goals: Raindrop effect from mouse click, 
//mesh noise add back in, 
//figure out what this pulse is
//aspect ratio of 
void main() {
    vec2 st = gl_FragCoord.xy / u_resolution.xy;
    // Generate one constant pseudo-random value.
    // Because the seed is always 10.1, rnd is the same for every pixel.
    float rnd = random(st);
    // Stores the final red, green, and blue channel values.
    vec3 c;
    // Will store the pixel's distance from the current origin.
    float l;
    // Start z at the current elapsed time.
    float z = t;
    // Run once for each RGB channel: i=0 red, i=1 green, i=2 blue.
    for(int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        // Shift coordinates so the mouse becomes the new origin.
    	// NOTE: because st is changed each loop, this shift accumulates.
    	st -= (u_mouse / r);

float targetAspect = 16.0 / 9.0;
float currentAspect = r.x / r.y;
float aspectCorrection = currentAspect / targetAspect;

st.x *= 0.3 * aspectCorrection;
        // Shift the phase differently for each RGB channel.
        // First loop: t-1, second: t-2, third: t-3.
        z -= 1.0;
        // Measure this pixel's distance from the current origin.
        // This radial distance is what allows circular/ring patterns.
        l = length(st);
        // Controls how tightly packed the radial rings are.
        float ringFrequency = 50.0;
        // Global oscillation over time: ranges approximately from -1 to 1.
    //float pulse = sin(t);

        // Create an oscillating wave based on both radial distance and time.
        // l controls WHERE the rings are; z makes them move over time.
        float radialWave = sin(l * ringFrequency - 2.0 * z);
        // Make the distortion stronger near the center and weaker farther away.
        float scale = rnd / 2.2;

        // Multiply the coordinates by the inverse of the combined distortion.
        // This warps st using distance, pulse, and the moving radial wave.
        st *= pow(scale * radialWave, -1.0);
        
        float band = fract(0.01 / length(st - 0.5));
        // Measure distance from (.5,.5), invert it to create a bright center,
        // then fract() wraps large values into repeating 0–1 bands.
        // Store the result in the current RGB channel.
        float fade = 5.0 / (1.0 + l * 3.0);

		c[i] = band * fade;
    }
    // Add radial distance l to every RGB channel, increasing brightness,
    // and output the final color with full opacity.
    gl_FragColor = vec4(c*9.0 + l, 1.0);
}
```

import * as THREE from '../vendor/three/three.module.js';

const renderer=new THREE.WebGLRenderer({canvas,antialias:true,alpha:false});
renderer.autoClear=false;renderer.setClearColor(0xffffff,1);renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio,2));
const scene=new THREE.Scene(),camera=new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(28,1,.1,20);camera.position.z=4;
camera.updateMatrixWorld();

 fetch(new URL('../effects/phantom-owl/owl-surface.glsl',import.meta.url)),
 fetch(new URL('../effects/phantom-color/phantom-color.glsl',import.meta.url)),
 fetch(new URL('../effects/phantom-owl/wing-deformation.glsl',import.meta.url))
]);
if(!response.ok||!colorResponse.ok||!vertexResponse.ok)throw new Error('Shader load failed');
const colorShader=await colorResponse.text();
const surfaceShader=(await response.text()).replace('#include <phantom_color>',colorShader);
const texture=await new THREE.TextureLoader().loadAsync(new URL('../assets/owls/barn-owl/generated/phantom-front-v1.png',import.meta.url).href);
texture.minFilter=THREE.LinearFilter;texture.magFilter=THREE.LinearFilter;texture.generateMipmaps=false;
const maps=buildSurfaceMaps(texture.image);
const uniforms={u_time:{value:0},u_resolution:{value:new THREE.Vector2(16,9)},u_owl:{value:texture},u_flap:{value:0},u_wrist:{value:0},u_depth:{value:0},u_depthTip:{value:0},u_wake:{value:new THREE.Vector2()},u_imageAspect:{value:maps.width/maps.height},u_normal:{value:maps.normal},u_relief:{value:maps.relief}};
uniforms.u_leftWing={value:new THREE.Vector4()};uniforms.u_rightWing={value:new THREE.Vector4()};uniforms.u_fold={value:new THREE.Vector2()};
const material=new THREE.ShaderMaterial({uniforms,transparent:true,depthTest:true,depthWrite:true,vertexShader:await vertexResponse.text(),fragmentShader:surfaceShader});
const owl=new THREE.Mesh(buildWingVolume(texture.image),material);owl.renderOrder=100;owl.frustumCulled=false;scene.add(owl);
const cloud=new CloudField(renderer,colorShader);
let simulationTime=0;
function resize(){renderer.setSize(innerWidth,innerHeight);const a=innerWidth/innerHeight;camera.aspect=a;camera.updateProjectionMatrix();const w=Math.min(a*1.4,2.3);owl.scale.set(w,w*maps.height/maps.width,w);cloud.resize(innerWidth,innerHeight);simulationTime=0;}
addEventListener('resize',resize);resize();
const reduce=matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
// Optional deterministic QA time; no controls/text in the visible experience.
const params=new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const fixed=params.get('time');
const seed=params.has('seed')?Number(params.get('seed')):(fixed===null?crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))[0]:12345);
const flightMotion=createFlightMotion(seed);
const wingWake=createWingWake(flightMotion);
let elapsed=0,previous=performance.now();

// 5, 6, or 7 completed flaps. Every downstroke keeps the same depth.

   tipKeys.push([end+duration+length*(.24+tipPhaseLag),upper],[end+duration+length*(.56+tipPhaseLag),lower]);

  distances[i]=d;
 }

  if(y<rows){d=Math.min(d,distances[i+stride]+dy);if(x>0)d=Math.min(d,distances[i+stride-1]+diagonal);if(x<columns)d=Math.min(d,distances[i+stride+1]+diagonal);}

uniform float u_flap;
uniform float u_wrist;
uniform float u_depth;
uniform float u_depthTip;
uniform vec4 u_leftWing;
uniform vec4 u_rightWing;
uniform vec2 u_fold;
uniform float u_imageAspect;
uniform sampler2D u_relief;
attribute float a_shell;
attribute float a_edge;
attribute float a_roundness;
varying float v_edge;
varying vec2 vUv;
void main(){
 v_edge=a_edge;
 vUv=uv;
 vec3 p=position;
 float span=abs(position.x);
 float wing=smoothstep(.065,.17,span);
 float reach=max(span-.085,0.0);
 float outer=smoothstep(.20,.48,span);
 vec4 stroke=position.x<0.0?u_leftWing:u_rightWing;
 float fold=position.x<0.0?u_fold.x:u_fold.y;
 float angle=mix(stroke.x,stroke.y,outer*.55);
 float depthAngle=mix(stroke.z,stroke.w,outer*.65);
 // Bend the image-derived wing shell at its shoulders. UV-attached colors and
 // surface maps travel with the feathers; the body/face remain anchored.
 p.x=mix(position.x,sign(position.x)*(.085+reach*cos(angle*.60)*cos(depthAngle)),wing);
 p.y+=reach*sin(angle)*u_imageAspect*wing*.68;
 p.z+=reach*sin(depthAngle)*wing;
 // A cambered, cupped surface: the wing has a rounded chord and flexible
 // trailing edge, rather than rotating as a rigid paper card.
 float chord=(uv.y-.56)/.39;
 float cup=max(0.0,1.0-chord*chord);
 float power=max(-stroke.x,0.0);
 float camber=cup*(.045+.075*power)*wing;
 float twist=(uv.y-.56)*outer*sin(angle)*.19*wing;
 float featherRelief=texture2D(u_relief,uv).r*.045*wing;
 p.z+=camber+twist+featherRelief;
 p.y+=cup*sin(angle)*outer*.075*u_imageAspect*wing;
 p.x-=sign(position.x)*cup*outer*power*.018*wing;
 p.x-=sign(position.x)*reach*fold*outer*.13*wing;
 p.z+=cup*fold*outer*.03*wing;
 // Finite depth between upper/lower skins, tapered toward outer feathers.
 // Offset follows the folded wing's normal so thickness reads edge-on too.
 float thickness=(.025+.055*(1.0-outer)+.018*power)*wing;
 float profile=(.35+.65*sqrt(max(0.0,cup)))*sqrt(a_roundness);

 p+=vec3(shellOffset.x,shellOffset.y*u_imageAspect,shellOffset.z);

import * as THREE from '../../vendor/three/three.module.js';

// Image-registered relief, NOT recovered anatomy. All maps share the exact
// source pixels and orientation; no independent AI-generated normal image.
export function buildSurfaceMaps(image) {
  const width=image.naturalWidth, height=image.naturalHeight;
  const canvas=document.createElement('canvas');canvas.width=width;canvas.height=height;
  const context=canvas.getContext('2d',{willReadFrequently:true});context.drawImage(image,0,0);
  const pixels=context.getImageData(0,0,width,height).data;
  const luminance=new Float32Array(width*height), relief=new Float32Array(width*height);
  const valid=(x,y)=>pixels[(y*width+x)*4+3]>180;
  for(let y=0;y<height;y++)for(let x=0;x<width;x++){
    const k=y*width+x, j=k*4;
    luminance[k]=(pixels[j]*0.2126+pixels[j+1]*0.7152+pixels[j+2]*0.0722)/255;
    if(!valid(x,y))continue;
    const u=(x+0.5)/width, v=1-(y+0.5)/height;
    // Hand-tuned broad volume for this front-facing image only; dimensions
    // are artistic choices. Feather/face relief comes from image contrast.
    const head=Math.exp(-(((u-.5)/.075)**2)-((v-.69)/.23)**2);
    const breast=Math.exp(-(((u-.5)/.068)**2)-((v-.43)/.27)**2);
    const wings=Math.exp(-(((v-.56)/.20)**2))*Math.exp(-(((u-.5)/.55)**2));
    relief[k]=0.52*head+0.35*breast+0.10*wings+0.045*luminance[k];
  }
  const data=new Uint8Array(width*height*4), heightData=new Uint8Array(width*height*4);
  // +X right, +Y up, +Z toward viewer. Alpha retains the source coverage.
  const step=2;
  for(let y=0;y<height;y++)for(let x=0;x<width;x++){
    const k=y*width+x,j=k*4;
    const sample=(sx,sy)=>valid(sx,sy)?relief[sy*width+sx]:relief[k];
    const left=Math.max(0,x-step),right=Math.min(width-1,x+step);
    const top=Math.max(0,y-step),bottom=Math.min(height-1,y+step);
    let nx=-(sample(right,y)-sample(left,y))*width/(right-left)*0.09;
    let ny=-(sample(x,top)-sample(x,bottom))*height/(bottom-top)*0.09;
    const inv=1/Math.hypot(nx,ny,1);
    data[j]=Math.round((nx*inv*.5+.5)*255);data[j+1]=Math.round((ny*inv*.5+.5)*255);data[j+2]=Math.round((inv*.5+.5)*255);data[j+3]=pixels[j+3];
    const h=Math.round(Math.min(1,relief[k])*255);
    heightData[j]=h;heightData[j+1]=Math.round(luminance[k]*255);heightData[j+2]=0;heightData[j+3]=pixels[j+3];
  }
  function texture(bytes){const t=new THREE.DataTexture(bytes,width,height,THREE.RGBAFormat);t.flipY=true;t.minFilter=THREE.LinearFilter;t.magFilter=THREE.LinearFilter;t.needsUpdate=true;return t;}
  return {normal:texture(data),relief:texture(heightData),width,height,
    provenance:'Image-registered approximate relief; broad volume is hand-tuned and fine relief is derived from luminance, not measured depth.'};
}

precision highp float;
uniform float u_time;
uniform vec2 u_wake;
uniform sampler2D u_owl;
uniform sampler2D u_normal;
uniform sampler2D u_relief;
uniform vec2 u_resolution;
varying vec2 vUv;
varying float v_edge;

#include <phantom_color>
void main(){
 vec2 uv=vUv;
 if(any(lessThan(uv,vec2(0)))||any(greaterThan(uv,vec2(1))))discard;
 vec4 owl=texture2D(u_owl,uv);
 float coverage=smoothstep(.55,.96,owl.a);
 if(coverage<.005)discard;
 vec3 normal=normalize(texture2D(u_normal,uv).xyz*2.0-1.0);
 vec2 surface=texture2D(u_relief,uv).rg;
 float clock=u_time*.075;
 // Smooth moving domains produce billowing regions instead of expanding rings.
 // Wake follows the shoulder-to-tip stroke path, not the face or body.
 float wingWeight=smoothstep(.075,.32,abs(uv.x-.5));
 float side=uv.x<.5?-1.0:1.0;
 vec2 shoulder=vec2(.5+side*.09,.60);
 vec2 radial=uv-shoulder;
 vec2 wakeShift=vec2(side*u_wake.y*.32,u_wake.x*.65)*wingWeight;
 wakeShift+=vec2(-radial.y,radial.x)*u_wake.y*wingWeight*.65;
 vec2 fieldUv=uv+wakeShift;
 vec2 p=fieldUv*vec2(2.0,1.3);
 vec2 flow=vec2(fbm(p+vec2(clock,-clock*.33)),fbm(p+vec2(-clock*.4,clock*.6)+9.2));
 float liquid=fbm(p*1.4+flow*2.3+vec2(-clock*.65,clock*.2));
 vec2 curved=fieldUv+(flow-.5)*.34+normal.xy*.028+vec2(0.0,surface.x*.09);
 // Contours follow a liquid density field, making closed flowing pools
 // rather than simply sweeping horizontal ripple bands across the bird.
 curved.y=mix(curved.y,.5+(liquid-.5)*0.42+normal.y*.03,.78);
 curved.y+=sin(clock*.7)*.05;
 // Three offset strand fields increase coverage without narrowing the strands.
 vec3 pigment=strandColor(curved,clock);
 // Broad pools are translucent; features appear only as the pools pass them.
 float pool=smoothstep(.30,.67,liquid);
 float feather=1.0-surface.y;
 float reliefEdge=length(normal.xy);
 float reveal=pool*(.28+.58*feather+.24*reliefEdge);
 // A second advected sample catches fine face/feather detail in the same
 // original spectrum, without adding a new palette or painting on a photograph.
 vec3 detailPigment=originalColor(vec2(curved.x, .50+(flow.y-.5)*.17),clock);
 // Stronger chromatic density; keep neutral feather detail unchanged.
 vec3 absorption=(1.0-pigment)*(.65+.35*reveal)*4.455;
 absorption+=(1.0-detailPigment)*feather*pool*.9801;
 // Neutral optical density reveals eye sockets and feather separations.
 // It does not recolor the spectrum or display the photo as an opaque skin.
 absorption+=vec3(feather*pool*.15);
 // White-dominant transmission matches the screenshots. No HSV boosts,
 // artificial lighting, replacement rainbow, or photographic RGB overlay.
 // Keep the same palette across the feather rim, with a subtle volume cue.
 vec3 color=1.0-clamp(absorption*(1.0+v_edge*.12),0.0,.7);
 float alpha=coverage*smoothstep(.23,.54,liquid);
 if(alpha<.005)discard;
 gl_FragColor=vec4(color,alpha);
}

// Original shader noise and RGB calculations. shaderRef.glsl stays untouched.
float random(vec2 st) { return fract(sin(dot(st,st))*43758.5453123); }
float hash(vec2 p){return fract(sin(dot(p,vec2(127.1,311.7)))*43758.5453);}
float noise(vec2 p){vec2 i=floor(p),f=fract(p);f=f*f*(3.0-2.0*f);
 return mix(mix(hash(i),hash(i+vec2(1,0)),f.x),mix(hash(i+vec2(0,1)),hash(i+vec2(1,1)),f.x),f.y);}
float fbm(vec2 p){return noise(p)*.57+noise(p*2.03+3.1)*.28+noise(p*4.01+7.7)*.15;}
vec3 originalColor(vec2 point,float time){
 vec2 st=point;float rnd=random(st);vec3 c=vec3(0);float l=0.0;float z=time;
 for(int i=0;i<3;i++){
   // Keep the original ACCUMULATING coordinates. Resetting here caused
   // the unwanted saturated rainbow in the previous version.
   st-=vec2(.5);
   st.x*=.3*(u_resolution.x/u_resolution.y)/(16.0/9.0);
   z-=1.0;l=length(st);
   float radialWave=sin(l*50.0-2.0*z);
   float scale=rnd/2.2;
   float denom=scale*radialWave;
   // Mathematically the original inverse, defined for negative inputs too.
   st*= (denom<0.0?-1.0:1.0)/max(abs(denom),.00001);
   float band=fract(.01/max(length(st-.5),.00001));
   float fade=5.0/(1.0+l*3.0);
   c[i]=band*fade;
 }
 return clamp(c*9.0+l,0.0,1.0);
}
// Keep a complete RGB sample when strand fields overlap.
vec3 strandColor(vec2 curved,float clock){
 vec3 pigment=originalColor(curved,clock);
 vec3 strandA=originalColor(curved+vec2(.08,.13+sin(clock*.43)*.025),clock+.65);
 vec3 strandB=originalColor(curved+vec2(-.07,-.13+cos(clock*.37)*.025),clock+1.3);
 vec3 densityWeights=vec3(.2126,.7152,.0722);
 if(dot(1.0-strandA,densityWeights)>dot(1.0-pigment,densityWeights))pigment=strandA;
 if(dot(1.0-strandB,densityWeights)>dot(1.0-pigment,densityWeights))pigment=strandB;
 return pigment;
}

import * as THREE from '../../vendor/three/three.module.js';
// A persistent advected velocity/color field. No stored wing images or ghost meshes.
export class CloudField {
 constructor(renderer,colorShader){
  this.renderer=renderer;
  this.camera=new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1);
  this.scene=new THREE.Scene();this.quad=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2,2),null);this.scene.add(this.quad);
  const vertexShader='varying vec2 vUv;void main(){vUv=uv;gl_Position=vec4(position.xy,0.0,1.0);}';
  const header=`precision highp float;varying vec2 vUv;uniform sampler2D u_velocity;uniform sampler2D u_dye;uniform sampler2D u_source;uniform vec2 u_texel;uniform float u_dt;uniform float u_time;uniform float u_aspect;uniform vec4 u_emitters[6];
  uniform float u_zero;
  vec2 decode(vec2 v){return (v-u_zero)*.9;}
  vec2 encode(vec2 v){return v/.9+u_zero;}
  vec2 metric(vec2 d){return d*vec2(u_aspect,1.0);}
  float airHash(vec2 p){return fract(sin(dot(p,vec2(127.1,311.7)))*43758.5453);}
  float airNoise(vec2 p){vec2 i=floor(p),f=fract(p);f=f*f*(3.0-2.0*f);
    return mix(mix(airHash(i),airHash(i+vec2(1,0)),f.x),mix(airHash(i+vec2(0,1)),airHash(i+vec2(1,1)),f.x),f.y);}
  `;
  const material=body=>new THREE.ShaderMaterial({vertexShader,fragmentShader:header+body,depthTest:false,depthWrite:false,uniforms:{u_zero:{value:.5},u_velocity:{value:null},u_dye:{value:null},u_source:{value:null},u_texel:{value:new THREE.Vector2()},u_dt:{value:0},u_time:{value:0},u_aspect:{value:1},u_emitters:{value:Array.from({length:6},()=>new THREE.Vector4())}}});
  // Write numerical RGBA directly; a translucent clear color is premultiplied
  // by the renderer and would corrupt both zero velocity and displacement.
  this.resetMaterial=material('void main(){gl_FragColor=vec4(u_zero);}');
  this.velocityMaterial=material(`void main(){
    vec2 vel=decode(texture2D(u_velocity,vUv).rg);
    vec2 back=clamp(vUv-vel*u_dt,0.001,0.999);
    vec4 carried=texture2D(u_velocity,back);
    vel=decode(carried.rg)*exp(-u_dt*1.05);
    for(int i=0;i<6;i++){
      vec2 delta=metric(vUv-u_emitters[i].xy);
      float speed=length(metric(u_emitters[i].zw));
      float falloff=exp(-dot(delta,delta)/.0045)*smoothstep(.01,.12,speed);
      vec2 force=clamp(u_emitters[i].zw*.80,vec2(-.32),vec2(.32));
      vel+= (force-vel)*falloff*(1.0-exp(-u_dt*5.5));
      // Tip-shed swirl carries and curls the disturbance rather than stamping shapes.
      vec2 tangent=vec2(-delta.y,delta.x)/max(length(delta),.015);
      float handed=i<3?1.0:-1.0;
      vel+=tangent/vec2(u_aspect,1.0)*handed*speed*falloff*u_dt*.95;
    }
    float energy=length(metric(vel));
    vec2 q=metric(vUv)*39.0+vec2(u_time*.38,-u_time*.31);
    vec2 curl=vec2(sin(q.x)*cos(q.y),-cos(q.x)*sin(q.y));
    vec2 fine=q*1.91+vec2(-u_time*.21,u_time*.27);
    curl+=vec2(sin(fine.x)*cos(fine.y),-cos(fine.x)*sin(fine.y))*.55;
    float mass=length(texture2D(u_dye,vUv).rgb);
    float occupied=smoothstep(.002,.08,mass);
    vel+=curl/vec2(u_aspect,1.0)*(energy*.85+.022*occupied)*u_dt;
    // Light ambient lift keeps shed wisps drifting after a wing reverses.
    vel+=vec2(.005*sin(u_time*.27)/u_aspect,.016)*occupied*u_dt;
    vel=clamp(vel,vec2(-.44),vec2(.44));
    // BA carries accumulated displacement, not instantaneous velocity.
    // Pigment travels with the air and never springs back to its old position.
    vec2 displacement=decode(carried.ba)+vel*u_dt;
    gl_FragColor=vec4(encode(vel),encode(clamp(displacement,vec2(-.44),vec2(.44))));
  }`);
  this.dyeMaterial=material(`void main(){
    vec2 vel=decode(texture2D(u_velocity,vUv).rg);
    vec2 back=clamp(vUv-vel*u_dt,0.001,0.999);
    vec3 dye=texture2D(u_dye,back).rgb;
    vec3 neighbors=(texture2D(u_dye,back+vec2(u_texel.x,0)).rgb+texture2D(u_dye,back-vec2(u_texel.x,0)).rgb+texture2D(u_dye,back+vec2(0,u_texel.y)).rgb+texture2D(u_dye,back-vec2(0,u_texel.y)).rgb)*.25;
    float breakup=airNoise(metric(back)*43.0+vec2(u_time*.24,-u_time*.35));
    dye=mix(dye,neighbors,1.0-exp(-u_dt*8.0))*exp(-u_dt*(.85+breakup*.6));
    float injection=0.0;
    for(int i=0;i<6;i++){
      vec2 d=metric(vUv-u_emitters[i].xy);
      float speed=length(metric(u_emitters[i].zw));
      injection+=exp(-dot(d,d)/.0120)*smoothstep(.012,.18,speed);
    }
    // Diffuse samples of the LIVE shader provide its existing color spectrum.
    // Only color mass enters the field; the owl silhouette is not retained.
    vec3 source=vec3(0.0);
    for(int x=-1;x<=1;x++)for(int y=-1;y<=1;y++)
      source+=1.0-texture2D(u_source,vUv+vec2(float(x),float(y))*u_texel*3.5).rgb;
    source/=9.0;
    float wisps=.45+.75*airNoise(metric(vUv)*57.0+vec2(u_time*.3,-u_time*.2));
    dye+=source*min(injection,1.5)*wisps*(1.0-exp(-u_dt*5.0));
    gl_FragColor=vec4(clamp(dye,0.0,.7),1.0);
  }`);
  this.displayMaterial=material(`
  uniform vec2 u_resolution;
  uniform vec4 u_owlFrame;
  ${colorShader}
  void main(){
    vec3 dye=texture2D(u_dye,vUv).rgb;
    vec2 displacement=decode(texture2D(u_velocity,vUv).ba);
    // Transported pigment controls density. Restore its fine color structure
    // with the SAME shader as the wings: diffusion must not mix it into brown.
    float mass=max(dye.r,max(dye.g,dye.b));
    float density=smoothstep(.004,.095,mass);
    vec2 transported=vUv-displacement;
    vec2 air=metric(transported)*37.0+vec2(u_time*.12,-u_time*.18);
    float pockets=airNoise(air)*.65+airNoise(air*2.07+5.3)*.35;
    float porous=smoothstep(.22,.70,pockets);
    density*=mix(porous,1.0,smoothstep(.14,.30,mass));
    vec2 fieldUv=(transported-u_owlFrame.xy)/u_owlFrame.zw+.5;
    float clock=u_time*.075;
    vec2 p=fieldUv*vec2(2.0,1.3);
    vec2 flow=vec2(fbm(p+vec2(clock,-clock*.33)),fbm(p+vec2(-clock*.4,clock*.6)+9.2));
    float liquid=fbm(p*1.4+flow*2.3+vec2(-clock*.65,clock*.2));
    vec2 curved=fieldUv+(flow-.5)*.34;
    curved.y=mix(curved.y,.5+(liquid-.5)*.42,.78);
    curved.y+=sin(clock*.7)*.05;
    vec3 absorption=(1.0-strandColor(curved,clock))*4.455;
    // Same optical-density ceiling and full core opacity as the wing bands.
    gl_FragColor=vec4(1.0-clamp(absorption,0.0,.7)*density,1.0);
  }`);
  this.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_resolution={value:new THREE.Vector2(16,9)};
  this.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_owlFrame={value:new THREE.Vector4(.5,.5,.7,.3)};
  this.resize(innerWidth,innerHeight);
 }
 setOwlFrame(x,y,width,height){
  // Establish a color scale once. Detached air is not pulled with the owl.
  if(!this.frameReady){this.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_owlFrame.value.set(x,y,width,height);this.frameReady=true;}
 }
 resize(width,height){
  this.aspect=width/height;this.width=512;this.height=Math.max(192,Math.min(768,Math.round(512/this.aspect)));
  const type=this.renderer.extensions.has('EXT_color_buffer_float')?THREE.HalfFloatType:THREE.UnsignedByteType;
  for(const material of [this.resetMaterial,this.velocityMaterial,this.dyeMaterial,this.displayMaterial])material.uniforms.u_zero.value=type===THREE.HalfFloatType?.5:128/255;
  const make=(depthBuffer=false)=>new THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(this.width,this.height,{type,minFilter:THREE.LinearFilter,magFilter:THREE.LinearFilter,depthBuffer,stencilBuffer:false});
  for(const t of [...(this.velocity||[]),...(this.dye||[]),this.source])t?.dispose();
  this.velocity=[make(),make()];this.dye=[make(),make()];this.source=make(true);this.reset();
 }
 pass(material,target){this.quad.material=material;this.renderer.setRenderTarget(target);this.renderer.render(this.scene,this.camera);}
 reset(){
  this.frameReady=false;
  const r=this.renderer;
  for(const target of this.velocity)this.pass(this.resetMaterial,target);
  r.setClearColor(0,1);for(const target of this.dye){r.setRenderTarget(target);r.clear();}
  r.setRenderTarget(null);r.setClearColor(0xffffff,1);
 }
 step(dt,time,emitters,renderOwl){
  this.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_time.value=time;
  this.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_aspect.value=this.aspect;
  const r=this.renderer;r.setRenderTarget(this.source);r.setClearColor(0xffffff,1);r.clear();renderOwl();
  const update=material=>{
   const u=material.uniforms;u.u_velocity.value=this.velocity[0].texture;u.u_dye.value=this.dye[0].texture;u.u_source.value=this.source.texture;
   u.u_texel.value.set(1/this.width,1/this.height);u.u_dt.value=dt;u.u_time.value=time;u.u_aspect.value=this.aspect;
   emitters.forEach((v,i)=>u.u_emitters.value[i].copy(v));
  };
  update(this.velocityMaterial);this.pass(this.velocityMaterial,this.velocity[1]);this.velocity.reverse();
  update(this.dyeMaterial);this.pass(this.dyeMaterial,this.dye[1]);this.dye.reverse();
  r.setRenderTarget(null);
 }
 render(renderOwl){
  const r=this.renderer;r.setRenderTarget(null);r.setClearColor(0xffffff,1);r.clear();
  this.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_dye.value=this.dye[0].texture;this.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_velocity.value=this.velocity[0].texture;this.pass(this.displayMaterial,null);

```javascript
// Reproduction check for the documented animation snapshot. Node.js 22+.
// Start a dedicated Chrome with --remote-debugging-port=9223 first.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import {mkdir,writeFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {join} from 'node:path';
import {tmpdir} from 'node:os';
import {createFlightMotion} from '../effects/phantom-owl/flight-motion.mjs';

function verifyMotion(){
 const counts=new Set();let pauses=0,beats=0,joins=0;
 for(const seed of [1,2,3,4,5,6,12345,98765]){
  const m=createFlightMotion(seed),twin=createFlightMotion(seed);m.sample(300);
  let count=0,previous=null;
  for(const segment of [...m.segments]){
   if(segment.kind==='flap'){
    assert(segment.beats.length>=1&&segment.beats.length<=3);count+=segment.beats.length;
    if(previous?.kind==='flap'){assert.equal(previous.end,segment.start);assert(m.sample(segment.start).velocity>.1);joins++;}
    for(const beat of segment.beats){
     const peak=m.sample(segment.start+beat.start+(beat.end-beat.start)*.56);
     assert(Math.abs(peak.depth+1.02*1.06*1.14)<1e-10);assert.deepEqual(peak.left,peak.right);beats++;
    }
   }else if(segment.start>0){
    assert(count>=5&&count<=7);counts.add(count);pauses++;count=0;
    assert(Math.abs(segment.end-segment.start-.85)<1e-10);
    for(const t of [segment.start+.01,(segment.start+segment.end)/2,segment.end-.01]){
     const p=m.sample(t);assert.equal(p.mode,'glide');assert.equal(p.stroke,0);assert.equal(p.wrist,0);
    }
   }
   for(const t of [segment.start,segment.end]){
    const a=m.sample(Math.max(0,t-1e-6)),b=m.sample(t+1e-6);
    for(const key of ['stroke','wrist','depth','depthTip','fold'])assert(Math.abs(a.left[key]-b.left[key])<.0001);
    assert(Math.abs(a.velocity-b.velocity)<.001);
   }
   previous=segment;
  }
  for(const t of [0,1,9,20,55,120,299])assert.deepEqual(m.sample(t),twin.sample(t));
 }
 assert.deepEqual([...counts].sort(),[5,6,7]);
 return {pauseAfter:[...counts].sort(),pausesChecked:pauses,fullDepthFlapsChecked:beats,continuousJoinsChecked:joins,pauseSeconds:.85};
}
const motionChecks=verifyMotion();
if(process.argv.includes('--motion-only')){console.log(JSON.stringify(motionChecks,null,2));process.exit(0);}
const base=process.argv[2]||'http://127.0.0.1:8000/app/';
const output=process.argv[3]||join(tmpdir(),'phantom-snapshot');
await mkdir(output,{recursive:true});
const pages=await(await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:9223/json')).json();
const page=pages.find(p=>p.type==='page');assert(page,'Open a page in the dedicated QA Chrome.');
const ws=new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
await new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{ws.addEventListener('open',resolve,{once:true});ws.addEventListener('error',reject,{once:true});});
let id=0;const pending=new Map(),errors=[];
ws.addEventListener('message',event=>{
 const msg=JSON.parse(event.data);
 if(msg.method==='Runtime.exceptionThrown')errors.push(msg.params.exceptionDetails);
 if(msg.method==='Log.entryAdded'&&msg.params.entry.level==='error')errors.push(msg.params.entry);
 if(msg.method==='Runtime.consoleAPICalled'&&msg.params.type==='error')errors.push(msg.params.args);
 if(msg.id){const p=pending.get(msg.id);if(p){pending.delete(msg.id);clearTimeout(p.timer);msg.error?p.reject(msg.error):p.resolve(msg.result);}}
});
function call(method,params={}){return new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{
 const key=++id,timer=setTimeout(()=>{pending.delete(key);reject(new Error('CDP timed out: '+method));},15000);
 pending.set(key,{resolve,reject,timer});ws.send(JSON.stringify({id:key,method,params}));
});}
async function evaluate(expression){const r=await call('Runtime.evaluate',{expression,returnByValue:true});if(r.exceptionDetails)throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.exceptionDetails));return r.result.value;}
try{
 await call('Log.clear');await call('Runtime.enable');await call('Log.enable');await call('Page.enable');
 await call('Network.enable');await call('Network.setCacheDisabled',{cacheDisabled:true});
 await call('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride',{width:1440,height:1000,deviceScaleFactor:1,mobile:false});
 const url=new URL(base);url.searchParams.set('time','0');url.searchParams.set('seed','12345');
 await call('Page.navigate',{url:url.href});
 let ready=false;
 for(let i=0;i<150;i++){await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,100));if(await evaluate('!!window.__owl')){ready=true;break;}}
 assert(ready,'App did not load: '+JSON.stringify(errors));
 await evaluate('__owl.renderer.setAnimationLoop(null)');
 const frames=await evaluate(`(()=>{
  const m=__owl.flightMotion;m.sample(30);
  const first=m.segments.find(s=>s.kind==='flap'),beat=first.beats[0];
  const pause=m.segments.find(s=>s.kind==='glide'&&s.start>0);
  const next=m.segments.find(s=>s.kind==='flap'&&s.start>=pause.end),b=next.beats[0];
  return [{name:'full-depth',time:first.start+beat.start+(beat.end-beat.start)*.56},
   {name:'recovery',time:first.start+beat.end},
   {name:'pause',time:(pause.start+pause.end)/2},
   {name:'resume',time:next.start+b.start+(b.end-b.start)*.56}];
 })()`);
 for(const f of frames){
  // Rebuild each wake from zero with the same <=1/30-second step sequence.
  await evaluate(`__owl.renderAt(0);__owl.renderAt(${f.time})`);
  const shot=await call('Page.captureScreenshot',{format:'png'});
  await writeFile(join(output,`phantom-${f.name}.png`),Buffer.from(shot.data,'base64'));
 }
 const desktop=await evaluate(`({source:[__owl.maps.width,__owl.maps.height],seed:__owl.seed,
  geometryVertices:__owl.owl.geometry.attributes.position.count,triangles:__owl.owl.geometry.index.count/3,
  finiteGeometry:Array.from(__owl.owl.geometry.attributes.position.array).every(Number.isFinite),
  cloudSize:[__owl.cloud.width,__owl.cloud.height],cloudTextureType:__owl.cloud.dye[0].texture.type,
  colorFrame:__owl.cloud.displayMaterial.uniforms.u_owlFrame.value.toArray(),
  programs:__owl.renderer.info.programs.map(p=>({runnable:p.diagnostics?.runnable??true})),
  text:document.body.innerText,background:getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor})`);
 assert.deepEqual(desktop.source,[2172,724]);assert(desktop.finiteGeometry);
 assert(desktop.colorFrame.every(Number.isFinite));assert(desktop.programs.every(p=>p.runnable));
 assert.equal(desktop.text,'');assert.equal(desktop.background,'rgb(255, 255, 255)');
 await call('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride',{width:390,height:844,deviceScaleFactor:1,mobile:true});
 await evaluate(`window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));__owl.renderAt(0);__owl.renderAt(${frames[0].time})`);
 const mobile=await call('Page.captureScreenshot',{format:'png'});
 await writeFile(join(output,'phantom-mobile.png'),Buffer.from(mobile.data,'base64'));
 const report={seed:12345,desktopViewport:[1440,1000],devicePixelRatio:1,mobileViewport:[390,844],frames,motionChecks,desktop,errors};
 await writeFile(join(output,'capture-manifest.json'),JSON.stringify(report,null,2)+'\n');
 console.log(JSON.stringify(report,null,2));assert.equal(errors.length,0);
}finally{ws.close();}

"""Refresh the standalone guide from approved source/assets; retain its prose.

Run from any directory: python3 /path/to/project/tools/rebuild-guide.py
Review prose and captures before recording changed effects or parameter values.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import re
import textwrap

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
GUIDE = ROOT / "docs/PHANTOM_OWL_RECREATION.md"
SOURCE_SECTION = "## 11. Complete exact source snapshot"
TEXT_FILES = [
    ("README.md", "markdown"),
    ("index.html", "html"),
    ("owl-flight/index.html", "html"),
    ("references/shaders/shaderRef.glsl", "glsl"),
    ("archive/README.md", "markdown"),
    ("archive/owl-flight/shader-original.glsl", "glsl"),
    ("app/index.html", "html"),
    ("app/main.js", "javascript"),
    ("effects/phantom-owl/flight-motion.mjs", "javascript"),
    ("effects/phantom-owl/wing-volume.mjs", "javascript"),
    ("effects/phantom-owl/wing-deformation.glsl", "glsl"),
    ("effects/phantom-owl/surface-maps.js", "javascript"),
    ("effects/phantom-owl/owl-surface.glsl", "glsl"),
    ("effects/phantom-color/phantom-color.glsl", "glsl"),
    ("effects/cloud-wake/cloud-field.mjs", "javascript"),
    ("tools/verify-snapshot.mjs", "javascript"),
    ("tools/verify-phantom.mjs", "javascript"),
    ("tools/rebuild-guide.py", "python"),
    ("assets/owls/barn-owl/README.md", "markdown"),
    ("assets/owls/barn-owl/generated/phantom-front-prompt.txt", "text"),
    ("assets/owls/barn-owl/maps/phantom-front-uv.json", "json"),
    ("assets/owls/barn-owl/maps/manifest.json", "json"),
    ("docs/previews/barn-owl/animation-v12/capture-manifest.json", "json"),
    ("vendor/three/THREE-LICENSE.txt", "text"),
]
BINARY_FILES = ["assets/owls/barn-owl/generated/phantom-front-v1.png"] + [
    "docs/previews/barn-owl/animation-v12/phantom-" + name + ".png"
    for name in ["full-depth", "recovery", "pause", "resume", "mobile"]
]


def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def source_block(path, language, content):
    longest = max((len(s) for s in re.findall(r"`+", content)), default=0)
    fence = chr(96) * max(3, longest + 1)
    return f"### `{path}`\n\n<!-- FILE: {path} -->\n{fence}{language}\n{content}\n{fence}\n"


def main():
    prose, separator, _ = GUIDE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").partition(SOURCE_SECTION)
    if not separator:
        raise ValueError("Guide is missing its complete-source section marker.")
    dependencies = [
        {"path": "vendor/three/" + name,
         "url": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/" + name,
         "sha256": sha((ROOT / "vendor/three" / name).read_bytes())}
        for name in ["three.module.js", "three.core.js"]
    ]
    manifest = {
        "format_version": 3,
        "snapshot_date": "2026-11-11",
        "snapshot": "pause-after-5-to-7-12",
        "project_layout": "organized-project-13",
        "description": "Same approved phantom owl effect in the organized project layout.",
        "files": {path: sha((ROOT / path).read_bytes())
                  for path in [p for p, _ in TEXT_FILES] + BINARY_FILES},
        "dependencies": dependencies,
        "source_image_dimensions": [2172, 724],
        "reference_seed": 12345,
        "reference_capture": "docs/previews/barn-owl/animation-v12/capture-manifest.json",
        "server_root": ".",
        "entry": "app/index.html",
        "compatibility_entry": "owl-flight/index.html",
        "runtime_external_network_required": False,
    }
    originals = [ROOT / "references/shaders/shaderRef.glsl",
                 ROOT / "archive/owl-flight/shader-original.glsl"]
    assert originals[0].read_bytes() == originals[1].read_bytes()
    blocks = [source_block(path, language, (ROOT / path).read_bytes().decode("utf-8"))
              for path, language in TEXT_FILES]
    blocks.append(source_block("recreation-manifest.json", "json",
                               json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"))
    assets = []
    fence = chr(96) * 3
    for path in BINARY_FILES:
        encoded = "\n".join(textwrap.wrap(base64.b64encode((ROOT / path).read_bytes()).decode(), 100))
        assets.append(f"<!-- BASE64_FILE: {path} -->\n{fence}base64\n{encoded}\n{fence}\n")
    intro = (
        SOURCE_SECTION + "\n\n"
        "The file-marked blocks contain exact current source bytes. The extractor preserves "
        "final newlines and verifies the manifest. Explanatory snippets above are not extracted. "
        "Longer fences protect source files that contain their own Markdown fences.\n\n"
        "The app loads the surface, shared-color, and wing-deformation GLSL files from `effects/`. "
        "The original shader under `references/` and its identical backup under `archive/` "
        "are preserved for comparison. `tools/rebuild-guide.py` can refresh this snapshot after "
        "an approved change, using the prose and reference assets in the restored project.\n\n"
    )
    asset_intro = (
        "## 12. Embedded assets — decode programmatically\n\n"
        "The exact owl PNG and five current reference renders follow. Decode this data with "
        "the extractor rather than loading it into model context. Only the owl PNG is a runtime "
        "texture; screenshots are visual references.\n\n"
    )
    GUIDE.write_text(prose + intro + "\n".join(blocks) + "\n" + asset_intro + "\n".join(assets), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({"guide": str(GUIDE.relative_to(ROOT)), "artifacts": len(manifest["files"]),
                      "dependencies": len(dependencies), "bytes": GUIDE.stat().st_size}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

### `assets/owls/barn-owl/README.md`

<!-- FILE: assets/owls/barn-owl/README.md -->
```markdown
# Barn owl assets

- `references/`: the unchanged original photograph.
- `generated/`: the active `phantom-front-v1.png`, earlier pose/turnaround sheets, and exact generation prompts.
- `maps/`: registered approximate normal/relief exports and their UV/provenance metadata. The app regenerates its data textures from the runtime PNG on load.
- `views.json` and `animation-references.json`: reference-sheet descriptions, review notes, and hashes. Their asset paths are relative to this species folder, except the explicit relative source path inside the UV JSON.

The runtime currently uses only `generated/phantom-front-v1.png`. Other sheets guide future work; they are not a reconstructed multiview mesh or finished animation atlas.

Rendered effect previews are in [docs/previews/barn-owl](../../../docs/previews/barn-owl/). The complete guide is [PHANTOM_OWL_RECREATION.md](../../../docs/PHANTOM_OWL_RECREATION.md).

```

### `assets/owls/barn-owl/generated/phantom-front-prompt.txt`

<!-- FILE: assets/owls/barn-owl/generated/phantom-front-prompt.txt -->
```text
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a single high-resolution photorealistic barn owl directly front-facing in level gliding flight, wings fully extended horizontally, full symmetrical wingspan and tail visible with at least 8 percent transparent margin on all sides. Reference 1 is the original individual barn owl: preserve its white heart-shaped facial disk, tiny ivory beak, deep dark eyes, fine white facial feathers and buff-gray speckled wings. Reference 2 shows its established flight poses; use only the FRONT LEVEL GLIDE pose as anatomy guidance, not the multi-image layout. ONE owl only, not a contact sheet. Camera exactly frontal and orthographic-style, no head turn, feet tucked. Detailed overlapping individual flight feathers, clearly defined facial disk and breast feathers. Broad neutral diffuse lighting, no directional cast shadows. Entire owl isolated on genuinely transparent background. No scenery, no cloud, no gray haze, no text, no graphic effects. Landscape composition. This will serve as the aligned silhouette and fine surface-detail input to an ephemeral light shader, so prioritize crisp actual owl features and uninterrupted feather anatomy.

```
